items.reasoning: The proposed frame in dimension two is V=diag(1,-1), placed in both available positions with the identity placement. Directly V^T V=I and det(V)=-1. Any matrix agreeing with every prescribed column is entrywise V, so there is no remaining completion freedom and no determinant-positive solution. This independently proves the negative conclusion and both of the first two rubric criteria. The strict theorem's proof obtains a label outside the placement image by finite-cardinality contradiction; its orientation step multiplies on the right by a single-column signFlip at that unused label. When r=N and the placement is injective, it is surjective, so exactly this step loses its witness. The reference answer correctly identifies that missing ingredient. The counterexample is an actual reflection; the informal determinant-minus-one terminology should be read as orientation reversal in general dimensions, not a classification of every improper orthogonal matrix as a single hyperplane reflection. The claim is failure of an unconditional extension guarantee, not failure for every full frame: a determinant-positive full frame and the empty N=0 frame already meet the orientation condition. No resource or algorithm guarantee is inferred. la-006 proves the universal strict-case repair and includes an obstruction explanation, so there is genuine subproblem overlap; la-011's requested explicit full-frame counterexample is not the same full contract as that constructive theorem or la-005's O(N) completion.

items.reasoning: For product indices (i,u),(j,v), the conjugate-transposed entry of S tensor X is conjugate(S(j,i) X(v,u))=S(i,j) X(u,v), using Hermiticity of each factor over the complex field. Thus (S tensor X)^dagger=S tensor X; the same calculation applies to T tensor I since I is Hermitian. Adjoint additivity then gives H^dagger=H. There is no multiplication S T or T S, so their commutator is irrelevant; one does not need simultaneous diagonalization. The complete tensor/add/identity closure proofs in the source justify the same generic argument, and its one-dimensional Hamiltonian theorem is a specialization using the already Hermitian S1 and S2 pieces. For necessity of the X premise, the given outer one-dimensional factors S=[1], T=[0] reduce H to X=[[0,1],[0,0]], whose adjoint has its nonzero entry at (1,0) instead of (0,1). This verifies the counterexample and all rubric requirements exactly. The total matrix dimension is the product of the two system dimensions; empty factor carriers make the equality vacuous but do not invalidate the nonempty counterexample. This is Hermitian closure, not positive semidefiniteness, a norm bound, block encoding or a Hamiltonian simulation implementation. be-107 is block-diagonal unitarity, and be-011 is a filler-phase cancellation defect in an LCU source: they have different predicates/conclusions despite sharing adjoints or Hamiltonian vocabulary.
